clue.text: Conscientious dad not out placing bets?

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
a batter who is not out is still in
staking money is placing bets

explanation.surface: A careful father who is keeping a punt going, or still at the crease, while gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone painstaking takes great care over details, the same quality as a diligent, conscientious worker.

clue.text: With quiet tread walk home

blocks.note: first meaning: to walk softly, as a cat does
second meaning: slang for one's flat or place to live

explanation.surface: Someone creeps home quietly, perhaps late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one instruction to tiptoe home; it splits into two separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb describes soft-footed walking, and the noun is informal slang for a person's flat or living quarters.

clue.text: One ready to cross loch and land in river?

indicators.note: to cross is to span something, so one pair of letters straddles another piece placed between them

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
set, as in ready, steady, go
L is a map abbreviation for loch or lake

explanation.surface: Someone poised to row over a Scottish loch and come ashore in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: I and SET run together, and SET wraps round the L.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a small island, and such a patch of ground is often found sitting midstream, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Pocketing a brown, so coming to black?

indicators.note: pocketing means putting something away inside, so one word holds the others within it

blocks.note: sic is Latin for so or thus, used to flag a quoted error
taken as written
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A snooker player pots the brown and so moves on to the black ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The snooker picture, with its brown and black balls, hides that black here means wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Black can mean evil or diabolical, and satanic describes something devilish and wicked in the same way.

clue.text: Last word about puzzle: Torquemada's First Surprise

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the closing word is wrapped round the puzzle
First asks for only the opening letter of the setter's name

blocks.note: amen is the word that ends a prayer
a maze is a puzzle of paths
the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A tribute headline: the final say on a crossword by Torquemada, his first big surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquemada was the pen name of the Observer's famous early crossword setter, which fits the puzzle surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazement is the feeling of great surprise or astonishment, so the noun replaces surprise directly.

clue.text: Start off well — pint making you clumsy?

indicators.note: with its start off, the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: fine means well, as in feeling fine
pt is the abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: Begin the evening well, but a pint later you are fumbling about.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill or awkward in handling things, close to clumsy; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Make merry: go further in mountain valley

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a glen is a narrow valley in the Scottish mountains
to add is to go further in what one says

explanation.surface: An instruction to hikers to have fun and push on deeper into the highland valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To gladden is to cheer someone up or make them happy, which is what make merry means here.

clue.text: Sun or Earth: one has to go!

indicators.note: has to go means a letter must leave the word

blocks.note: soil is earth, the ground
the Roman numeral for one, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A cosmic ultimatum: either the sun or the planet must be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Sun and Earth look like a pair of planets to choose between; Earth is just soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sol is the Latin name for the sun, used in astronomy and poetry for our star.

clue.text: For all that, long sentence offers pleasing image?

blocks.note: still means nevertheless, for all that
a life sentence is the longest prison term

explanation.surface: Despite a lengthy prison stretch, a convict manages a cheering picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A still life is a painting of arranged objects such as fruit or flowers, a kind of pleasing picture.

clue.text: Deception and appalling greed in male

indicators.note: something appalling is a dreadful mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint about trickery and shocking avarice found in a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Legerdemain is sleight of hand, so by extension any trickery or deception.

clue.text: Vessels from Holland draw fleet out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their usual order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ships from the Netherlands pull the navy out to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessels and fleet suggest ships; the vessels are pots and dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Delftware is the blue-and-white glazed pottery made in Delft, so Dutch vessels in the sense of jugs and bowls.

clue.text: Opposed to gang's leader, or getting on?

indicators.note: a leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: agin is a dialect word meaning against
the opening letter of gang

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you oppose the ringleader or are just growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing older, which is what an ageing person is doing.

clue.text: Money put into eg West End's opening show?

indicators.note: put into means placed inside, so the cash goes within the name
an opening is the start, so just the first letter is taken

blocks.note: Mae West, the film star, is an example of a West
tin is slang for money
the opening letter of End

explanation.surface: Investors back a West End production on its first night.
explanation.walkthrough: West End looks like London's theatre district; West is a surname, as in Mae West.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance of a play, a kind of theatrical show.

clue.text: Wealthy sort one in mineral oil refinement?

indicators.note: refinement processes crude material into a new form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rich person made a fortune in oil refining.
explanation.walkthrough: The one is placed in among the oil letters before the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A millionaire is someone with a fortune of a million or more, a typical rich person.

clue.text: Short drink relative knocked back, little one

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the drink loses its final letter
knocked back means pushed backwards, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

blocks.note: a toddy is a hot drink of spirits, sugar and water
rel is an abbreviation for relative

explanation.surface: A relative downs a small drink while the little one watches.
explanation.walkthrough: Knocked back looks like drinking, but it reverses only the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler is a young child learning to walk, commonly called a little one.

clue.text: London theatre players itch occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the even-placed letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Actors at a London theatre get the occasional itch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lyric is a theatre on Shaftesbury Avenue in London's West End; there is another in Hammersmith.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lyric is the name of a well-known playhouse in the capital, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Steps taken to bring about downfall

definitions.text: Steps taken to bring about downfall

blocks.clueFragment: Steps taken to bring about downfall
blocks.note: surface reading: measures taken to cause someone's ruin

blocks.clueFragment: Steps taken to bring about downfall
blocks.note: setter's reading: dance steps performed to make a downpour of water from the sky

explanation.walkthrough: Downfall looks like ruin and steps like measures; read literally they are dance steps and falling weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain dance is a ritual dance performed to summon precipitation, so its steps aim to bring about a downpour.

clue.text: Lover dropped in — see TV set that's wide

indicators.note: set means arranged, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner, a lover who has been dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old flame drops by to look at a widescreen television.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropped in looks like a visit; dropped belongs to the lover, and in joins the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Extensive means covering a large area or range, so it is a synonym of wide.

clue.text: Newsreader once in row involving personal credit

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the row wraps round the other letters

blocks.note: a tier is a row of seats
own means personal, belonging to oneself
CR is the abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A former news presenter got into a row over a personal loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Before newspapers a town crier called out public announcements in the street, a historic reader of news.

clue.text: Woman fell holding stone dish

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the felling word grips the weight unit

blocks.note: Iris is a woman's name
to hew is to fell or chop down
st is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A woman trips while carrying a heavy stone serving plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Fell looks like a past-tense fall; here it is the verb to chop down.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish stew is a traditional casserole of mutton, potatoes and onions, a kind of dish.

clue.text: Male cat catches cold, in a wind

indicators.note: catches means grabs and holds, so the big cat takes the cold letter inside

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
a lion is a big cat
C stands for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A tomcat comes down with a chill out in a breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: Wind looks like a breeze; it is short for a wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicon is a large circular tuba worn round the body, a brass wind instrument.

clue.text: Pagan deity priest continually repelled

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the word for always is read backwards

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
aye is an old word meaning always or forever

explanation.surface: A clergyman keeps warding off a heathen god.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse goddess of love and fertility, worshipped by the pre-Christian Scandinavians.

clue.text: Marsh in fine country, not good

indicators.note: not good asks for the abbreviation for good to be taken away

blocks.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
a country of the UK

explanation.surface: A boggy area in a pleasant country that is nonetheless no good.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are low-lying former marshland in eastern England, which makes the surface fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenland is flat, wet low-lying ground, essentially marshland or fen country.

clue.text: Unload bananas, ripe on one side with lumps

indicators.note: going bananas is going crazy, so the letters are scrambled
on one side means only the edge of the word, its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of ripe

explanation.surface: Offload the ripe bananas, which are lumpy on one side.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas looks like the fruit being unloaded; it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodular means having nodules, small rounded lumps, so it describes something lumpy.

clue.text: Borders outside close to free French city

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the edges go round the inner letter
close to means the end, so only the last letter is wanted

blocks.note: rims are edges or borders
the final letter of free

explanation.surface: Frontiers lie beyond a city near the free zone of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Reims is a city in the Champagne region of north-eastern France, famed for its cathedral.

clue.text: Check on time for charging first murderer

indicators.note: charging means loading or filling, so the murderer is filled with the other letters

blocks.note: Cain killed Abel, the first murder in the Bible
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An inquiry into whether the first killer was charged on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Charging looks legal; it means filling, like charging a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain a fire or an advance is to hold it back, so contain means to check or restrain.

clue.text: Man after a kiss in principle

blocks.note: taken as written
X is the kiss written at the end of a letter
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man who comes after a kiss, in theory at least.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, the island between Britain and Ireland; after places it behind the A and kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement accepted as self-evidently true, a basic principle or rule.

clue.text: Mocking but not right, like some columns

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the letter for right is taken away

blocks.note: ironic means mocking, saying the opposite
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A taunting remark that is wrong, like some newspaper columns.
explanation.walkthrough: Columns suggests journalism; they are the pillars of classical architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, known for scroll-shaped capitals on its pillars.

clue.text: One musical man returning is unoriginal

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the show and the name are read backwards

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
Tim is a man's name

explanation.surface: A songwriter who keeps coming back with the same tunes lacks originality.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Tim Rice wrote the lyrics for Evita, so the musical man is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitative means copying others, so it describes work that is derivative and lacks originality.

clue.text: Goddess, Greek god and Aesop in the middle?

indicators.note: in the middle asks for the central letter of each word

blocks.note: the central letter of the five
the central letter of the three
the central letter of the five

explanation.surface: Was a goddess among the Greek gods and Aesop's fables?
explanation.definitionFit: Eos is the Greek goddess of the dawn, sister of Helios the sun.

clue.text: Name dropped by fair lady in garden

indicators.note: dropped by means let go by, so the word loses the letter for name

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
even means fair, as in an even contest

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman in a garden forgets someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair lady reads as a phrase; fair belongs to the wordplay and lady to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve was the first woman, living in the Garden of Eden in the Bible.

clue.text: Mum rushes around to stop wit becoming prophet

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the two words are read backwards
to stop is to plug a gap, so these letters fill the middle of the word for wit

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
darts means dashes or rushes
nous is common sense or wit

explanation.surface: A mother dashes about to silence a joker who is turning into a seer.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum looks like silence, as in keep mum; here it is mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostradamus was the 16th-century French astrologer famous for his book of predictions, the archetypal seer.
